construct: During sustained metabolic acidosis, proximal-tubule cells increase glutamine uptake and metabolism. Glutamine metabolism generates ammonium for urinary acid excretion and bicarbonate that is returned to the blood. Excretion of the generated ammonium therefore adds new bicarbonate to the body and is a major adaptive renal response to acid loading.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Sustained metabolic acidosis increases proximal-tubule glutamine metabolism; this generates ammonium for urinary excretion and new bicarbonate returned to blood.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Alpha-intercalated-cell H+-ATPase activity is a real compensatory acid-secretory response, but it does not generate the ammonium pool identified in the stem.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The question asks the metabolic source of increased urinary ammonium, which uniquely points to proximal-tubule glutamine metabolism.
